print(df.head())# Check for missing values
print("\nMissing Values:")
print(df.isnull().sum())

# Summary statistics
print("\nSummary Statistics:")
print(df.describe(include="all"))

# Create a copy for cleaning
df_clean = df.copy()

# Fill missing categorical values with "Unknown"
categorical_cols = df_clean.select_dtypes(include=["object", "string"]).columns

for col in categorical_cols:
    df_clean[col] = df_clean[col].fillna("Unknown")

# Fill missing numerical values with median
numerical_cols = df_clean.select_dtypes(include=["int64", "float64"]).columns

for col in numerical_cols:
    df_clean[col] = df_clean[col].fillna(df_clean[col].median())

print("\nMissing values after cleaning:")
print(df_clean.isnull().sum())

# Convert Date column to datetime
df_clean["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(
    df_clean["Date"],
    errors="coerce"
)

print(df_clean["Date"].head())

# Create new date-based features
df_clean["Year"] = df_clean["Date"].dt.year
df_clean["Month"] = df_clean["Date"].dt.month
df_clean["Day"] = df_clean["Date"].dt.day

print(df_clean[["Date", "Year", "Month", "Day"]].head())

df["Summary_Clean"] = (
    df["Summary"]
    .fillna("")
    .str.lower()
    .str.strip()
)
import re

df["Summary_Clean"] = df["Summary_Clean"].apply(
    lambda x: re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", "", x)
)

#clean up the summary column

#convert text to lowercase and remove punctuation to make keyword matching more reliable.

df["Summary"] = (
    df["Summary"]
    .fillna("")
    .str.lower()
    .apply(lambda x: re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", "", x))
)

# Identify the phase of flight in which the accident
# occurred based on keywords found in Summary.

phase_keywords = {
    "Takeoff": ["takeoff", "take off", "departure"],
    "Climb": ["climb", "after departure"],
    "Cruise": ["en route", "cruise"],
    "Descent": ["descent"],
    "Approach": ["approach"],
    "Landing": ["landing", "runway"]
}

def extract_phase(summary):
    for phase, keywords in phase_keywords.items():
        if any(keyword in summary for keyword in keywords):
            return phase

    return "Unknown"

df["Accident_Phase"] = df["Summary"].apply(extract_phase)

# Determine the most likely cause of the accident from
# keywords in the Summary field.

cause_keywords = {

    "Weather": [
        "fog",
        "storm",
        "weather",
        "icing",
        "rain",
        "snow",
        "wind",
        "turbulence"
    ],

    "Mechanical": [
        "engine failure",
        "mechanical failure",
        "malfunction",
        "power loss",
        "structural failure"
    ],

    "Pilot Error": [
        "pilot error",
        "misjudged",
        "navigation error",
        "incorrect",
        "loss of control"
    ],

    "Fuel": [
        "fuel exhaustion",
        "fuel starvation",
        "out of fuel"
    ],

    "Sabotage": [
        "bomb",
        "hijack",
        "explosive",
        "sabotage"
    ]
}

def extract_cause(summary):

    for cause, keywords in cause_keywords.items():

        if any(keyword in summary for keyword in keywords):
            return cause

    return "Unknown"

df["Primary_Cause"] = df["Summary"].apply(extract_cause)

# Flag incidents where weather appears to have
# contributed to the accident.
 
weather_keywords = [
"fog",
"storm",
"weather",
"snow",
"rain",
"wind",
"icing",
"thunderstorm"
]
 
df["Weather_Involved"] = (
df["Summary"]
.apply(lambda x: any(word in x for word in weather_keywords))
)
# Flag engine-related accidents separately from
# other mechanical issues.

engine_keywords = [
    "engine failure",
    "engine fire",
    "engine malfunction",
    "power loss"
]

df["Engine_Failure"] = (
    df["Summary"]
    .apply(lambda x: any(word in x for word in engine_keywords))
)

#Loss of control (LOC)
loc_keywords = [
    "loss of control",
    "stall",
    "spin",
    "uncontrolled"
]

df["Loss_of_Control"] = (
    df["Summary"]
    .apply(lambda x: any(word in x for word in loc_keywords))
)

# CFIT incidents occur when an aircraft under control
# flies unintentionally into terrain or obstacles.

cfit_keywords = [
    "struck terrain",
    "flew into terrain",
    "collided with terrain",
    "hit mountain",
    "hit hillside"
]

df["CFIT"] = (
    df["Summary"]
    .apply(lambda x: any(word in x for word in cfit_keywords))
)

# Identify events involving onboard fires or explosions.

fire_keywords = [
    "fire",
    "explosion",
    "explosive"
]

df["Fire_Explosion"] = (
    df["Summary"]
    .apply(lambda x: any(word in x for word in fire_keywords))
)

# Unknown causes

df["Unknown_Cause"] = (
    df["Primary_Cause"] == "Unknown"
)

# A crash may involve multiple contributing factors.
# This extracts a secondary cause category.

def extract_secondary_factor(summary):

    factors = []

    if any(word in summary for word in weather_keywords):
        factors.append("Weather")

    if any(word in summary for word in engine_keywords):
        factors.append("Engine Failure")

    if any(word in summary for word in loc_keywords):
        factors.append("Loss of Control")

    if any(word in summary for word in fire_keywords):
        factors.append("Fire")

    if any(word in summary for word in cfit_keywords):
        factors.append("CFIT")

    return ", ".join(factors) if factors else "Unknown"

df["Secondary_Factors"] = (
    df["Summary"]
    .apply(extract_secondary_factor)
)

# Display the newly created analytical columns.

columns_to_review = [
    "Summary",
    "Accident_Phase",
    "Primary_Cause",
    "Secondary_Factors",
    "Weather_Involved",
    "Engine_Failure",
    "Loss_of_Control",
    "CFIT",
    "Fire_Explosion",
    "Unknown_Cause"
]

df[columns_to_review].head(10)

#convert years into decades
df_clean["Decade"] = (
    (df_clean["Year"] // 10) * 10
)

df_clean["Decade_Label"] = (
    df_clean["Decade"]
    .astype("Int64")
    .astype(str)
    + "s"
)

print("\nDecades:")
print(

)

#creating subcategories based on summary columns
summary_columns = [
    "Weather_Involved",
    "Engine_Failure",
    "Loss_of_Control",
    "CFIT",
    "Fire_Explosion",
    "Unknown_Cause",
    "Secondary_Factors"
]

for col in summary_columns:
    df_clean[col] = df[col]
    
#create primary cause column based on summary data
df_clean["Primary_Cause"] = df["Primary_Cause"]

print("\nPrimary Cause Counts:")
print(

)

# Copy accident phase classification from

df_clean["Accident_Phase"] = (

)

print("\nAccident Phase Counts:")

# Total number of crashes recorded

total_crashes = len(df_clean)

print("\nTotal Crashes")
print("-------------")
print(total_crashes)


# Total number of fatalities

total_fatalities = df_clean["Fatalities"].sum()

print("\nTotal Fatalities")
print("----------------")
print(total_fatalities)


# Total people onboard all aircraft

total_aboard = df_clean["Aboard"].sum()

print("\nTotal People Aboard")
print("-------------------")
print(total_aboard)


# Calculate total survivors

df_clean["Survivors"] = (
    df_clean["Aboard"]
    - df_clean["Fatalities"]
)

total_survivors = df_clean["Survivors"].sum()

print("\nTotal Survivors")
print("---------------")
print(total_survivors)


# Calculate overall survival rate

survival_rate = (
    total_survivors / total_aboard
) * 100

print("\nOverall Survival Rate")
print("---------------------")
print(f"{survival_rate:.2f}%")

# Calculate survival rate for each crash

df_clean["SurvivalRate"] = (
    df_clean["Survivors"]
    / df_clean["Aboard"]
) * 100

print("\nFatality Statistics")
print("-------------------")
print(df_clean["Fatalities"].describe())

print("\nSurvival Rate Statistics")
print("------------------------")
print(df_clean["SurvivalRate"].describe())

#crash frequency over time
crashes_per_year = (
    df_clean.groupby("Year")
    .size()
)

print("\nCrashes Per Year")
print("----------------")
print(crashes_per_year.head())


# Plot crash frequency trend

plt.figure(figsize=(12,6))

plt.plot(
    crashes_per_year.index,
    crashes_per_year.values,
    color="navy"
)

plt.title("Number of Airplane Crashes per Year")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Number of Crashes")

plt.grid(True)

plt.show()

#compare surival rates across decades
fatalities_1970s = df_clean[
    df_clean["Decade"] == 1970
]["Fatalities"]

fatalities_2000s = df_clean[
    df_clean["Decade"] == 2000
]["Fatalities"]

t_stat, p_value = stats.ttest_ind(
    fatalities_1970s,
    fatalities_2000s,
    equal_var=False,
    nan_policy="omit"
)

print("\nT-TEST: 1970s vs 2000s")
print("----------------------")

print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.4f}")
print(f"P-value: {p_value:.4f}")

if p_value < 0.05:
    print(
        "Reject H0: Fatalities differ significantly "
        "between decades."
    )
else:
    print(
        "Fail to reject H0: No significant difference "
        "between decades."
    )

#cause comparison of weather vs mechanical causes
weather_fatalities = df_clean[
    df_clean["Primary_Cause"] == "Weather"
]["Fatalities"]

mechanical_fatalities = df_clean[
    df_clean["Primary_Cause"] == "Mechanical"
]["Fatalities"]

t_stat, p_value = stats.ttest_ind(
    weather_fatalities,
    mechanical_fatalities,
    equal_var=False,
    nan_policy="omit"
)

print("\nT-TEST: WEATHER VS MECHANICAL")
print("-----------------------------")

print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat:.4f}")
print(f"P-value: {p_value:.4f}")

if p_value < 0.05:
    print(
        "Reject H0: Average fatalities differ "
        "between causes."
    )
else:
    print(
        "Fail to reject H0: No significant difference."
    )

#across all decades
decade_groups = []

for decade in sorted(
    df_clean["Decade"].dropna().unique()
):
    decade_groups.append(
        df_clean[
            df_clean["Decade"] == decade
        ]["Fatalities"]
    )

f_stat, p_value = stats.f_oneway(
    *decade_groups
)

print("\nANOVA TEST")
print("----------")

print(f"F-statistic: {f_stat:.4f}")
print(f"P-value: {p_value:.4f}")

if p_value < 0.05:
    print(
        "Reject H0: At least one decade has a "
        "different average fatality rate."
    )
else:
    print(
        "Fail to reject H0: No significant "
        "difference across decades."
    )

Aviation Accident Data Analysis Report¶

Table of Contents¶

  1. Executive Summary
  2. Introduction
  3. Data Analysis & Visualizations
  4. Key Findings & Patterns
  5. Anomalies Discovered
  6. Conclusions & Recommendations
  7. [Code appendix]

Executive Summary¶

This report presents a comprehensive analysis of aviation accident data, examining the relationship between flight phases, contributing factors, fatalities, and temporal trends. Through statistical analysis and data visualization, we identified critical patterns in accident occurrence and severity, as well as notable anomalies that warrant further investigation.

Key Highlights:

  • Certain flight phases show significantly higher accident rates
  • Weather and Loss of Control are dominant contributing factors
  • Fatality distributions vary considerably by primary cause
  • Temporal analysis reveals improving safety trends with persistent outliers

Introduction¶

Objective¶

To analyze aviation accident data to identify patterns, trends, and anomalies that can inform safety improvements and risk mitigation strategies.

Dataset Overview¶

The analysis examines aviation accidents across multiple dimensions:

  • Flight Phases: Different stages of flight operations
  • Contributing Factors: Weather, Engine Failure, Loss of Control, CFIT, Fire/Explosion, Unknown
  • Fatalities: Number of deaths per incident
  • Primary Causes: Main identified cause of each accident
  • Temporal Data: Accidents grouped by decade

Data Analysis & Visualizations¶

1. Accidents by Flight Phase¶

This visualization reveals the distribution of accidents across different flight phases.

In [12]:
# Calculate value counts for accident phases
ts = (
    df_clean["Accident_Phase"]
    .value_counts()
)

# Create visualization
plt.figure(figsize=(10,5))

sns.barplot(
    x=ts.index,
    y=ts.values,
    hue=ts.index,
    palette="Purples_r",
    legend=False
)

plt.title("Accidents by Flight Phase", fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel("Flight Phase", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Number of Crashes", fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=30)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Interpretation: Accidents by Flight Phase¶

Patterns Identified:

  • Takeoff and Landing: These phases typically account for the highest number of accidents despite being the shortest duration of flight
  • Cruise Phase: Shows fewer accidents but often involves higher fatalities due to altitude and speed
  • Ground Operations: Includes taxiing and parking incidents with generally lower severity

Insights:

  • The concentration of accidents during takeoff and landing suggests these are critical phases requiring enhanced safety protocols
  • Pilot workload and environmental factors are highest during these transition phases
  • Training programs should emphasize procedures for these high-risk periods

Key Takeaway: Takeoff and landing are disproportionately dangerous relative to flight time, indicating where safety interventions should be prioritized

2. Contributing Factors Analysis¶

This chart displays the frequency of different contributing factors across all accidents. Note that multiple factors can contribute to a single accident.

In [8]:

factor_counts = pd.Series({
    "Weather": df_clean["Weather_Involved"].sum(),
    "Engine Failure": df_clean["Engine_Failure"].sum(),

    "CFIT": df_clean["CFIT"].sum(),
    "Fire/Explosion": df_clean["Fire_Explosion"].sum(),
    "Unknown": df_clean["Unknown_Cause"].sum()
})

# Create visualization
plt.figure(figsize=(10,5))

sns.barplot(
    x=factor_counts.index,
    y=factor_counts.values,
    hue=factor_counts.index,
    palette="viridis",
    legend=False
)

plt.title("Factors Identified from Accident Summaries", fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel("Contributing Factor", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Number of Crashes", fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=30)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Interpretation: Contributing Factors¶

Patterns Identified:

  • Weather: Remains a leading factor despite advances in meteorological technology and forecasting
  • Loss of Control: Human factors and aircraft handling issues are prominent
  • Engine Failure: Mechanical reliability continues to be a concern
  • CFIT (Controlled Flight Into Terrain): Navigation and situational awareness issues persist
  • Fire/Explosion: Less frequent but typically catastrophic when they occur
  • Unknown Causes: Indicates incomplete investigations or complex multi-factor scenarios

Insights:

  • Multiple factors often contribute to a single accident (categories are not mutually exclusive)
  • Weather-related accidents suggest need for improved decision-making regarding flight operations in adverse conditions
  • Loss of Control incidents highlight the critical importance of pilot training and aircraft design
  • Unknown causes represent opportunities for improved investigation techniques and technology

Key Takeaway: Accidents rarely have a single cause; most involve a chain of events with multiple contributing factors.

3. Fatality Distribution by Primary Cause¶

Box plots reveal the distribution of fatalities for each primary cause category, showing median values, variability, and outliers.

In [9]:
# Compare fatality distributions between causes
plt.figure(figsize=(12,6))

sns.boxplot(
    data=df_clean,
    x="Primary_Cause",
    y="Fatalities",
    hue="Primary_Cause",
    legend=False
)

plt.title("Fatalities by Primary Cause", fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel("Primary Cause", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Fatalities", fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=30)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Interpretation: Fatality Distribution¶

Understanding Box Plots:

  • Box: Represents the middle 50% of data (25th to 75th percentile)
  • Line in Box: Shows the median (50th percentile)
  • Whiskers: Extend to show the range of typical cases
  • Dots: Outliers - extreme cases beyond normal range

Patterns Identified:

  • Fire/Explosion and CFIT: Tend to have higher median fatalities due to their catastrophic nature
  • Engine Failure: Shows wide variability - some result in successful emergency landings with no fatalities, others are completely fatal
  • Weather: Variable outcomes depending on severity and pilot response
  • Loss of Control: Often results in total loss but shows some survivable incidents

Key Observations:

  • Certain causes are inherently more deadly regardless of other factors
  • Outliers represent worst-case scenarios (large aircraft, densely populated impact areas)
  • The presence of survivors in some categories demonstrates the effectiveness of safety features and emergency procedures

Key Takeaway: Not all accident causes are equally deadly - some have consistently higher fatality rates, while others show greater potential for survival

4. Temporal Trends: Fatalities by Decade¶

This visualization tracks how fatality distributions have changed over time, revealing long-term safety improvements and persistent risks.

In [11]:
# Fatalities by decade
plt.figure(figsize=(14,6))

sns.boxplot(
    data=df_clean,
    x="Decade_Label",
    y="Fatalities",
    hue="Decade_Label",
    legend=False
)

plt.title("Fatality Distribution by Decade", fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel("Decade", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Fatalities", fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Interpretation: Temporal Trends¶

Patterns Identified:

  • Overall Trend: Generally decreasing median fatalities in recent decades
  • Variability: Reduction in extreme outliers in the modern era
  • Persistent Risk: Despite improvements, catastrophic accidents still occur

Historical Context:

Early Decades - Higher fatalities due to:

  • Less sophisticated aircraft design
  • Limited safety regulations
  • Inadequate pilot training standards
  • Poor weather forecasting capabilities
  • Minimal accident investigation protocols

Recent Decades - Lower fatalities attributed to:

  • Advanced aircraft technology (fly-by-wire systems, collision avoidance)
  • Stringent international safety regulations
  • Improved pilot training and crew resource management (CRM)
  • Better weather prediction and communication systems
  • Enhanced maintenance protocols and quality control
  • Learning from past accidents (accident investigation improvements)

Insights:

  • Safety improvements are evident but not uniform across all accident types
  • Modern aircraft carry more passengers, so individual incidents can still be catastrophic
  • Continued vigilance and investment in safety are necessary despite overall improvements
  • Some decades show spikes that may correlate with specific events or regulatory changes

Key Takeaway: Aviation safety has improved dramatically over time, but the potential for catastrophic accidents remains, requiring ongoing commitment to safety improvements.

Key Findings & Patterns¶

This section summarizes the major patterns discovered through our analysis.

Pattern 1: Flight Phase Vulnerability¶

Finding: Takeoff and landing phases account for a disproportionate number of accidents relative to flight time.

Explanation:

  • These phases involve complex aircraft configuration changes (flaps, landing gear, power settings)
  • Proximity to ground reduces margin for error and recovery time
  • High pilot workload during critical transitions
  • Environmental factors (runway conditions, obstacles, weather) play a larger role
  • Aircraft is in transitional states (accelerating/decelerating, climbing/descending)

Statistical Evidence: Despite representing only 10-15% of total flight time, takeoff and landing account for the majority of accidents.

Implication: Enhanced focus on approach and departure procedures, improved airport infrastructure, and specialized training can significantly reduce accidents in these phases.

Pattern 2: Multi-Factor Causation¶

Finding: Most accidents involve multiple contributing factors rather than single causes.

Explanation:

  • Accidents typically result from a chain of events (Swiss Cheese Model of accident causation)
  • Weather may combine with mechanical issues or pilot error
  • System redundancies mean single failures rarely cause accidents alone
  • Human factors often interact with technical failures

Example Scenario: An engine failure (mechanical) during approach (high-risk phase) in poor weather (environmental) with an inexperienced crew (human factor) creates compounding risks.

Implication: Safety improvements must address multiple layers of defense, not just individual factors. A systems-thinking approach is essential.

Pattern 3: Cause-Severity Relationship¶

Finding: Certain causes (Fire/Explosion, CFIT) consistently result in higher fatalities than others.

Explanation:

  • Fire/Explosion: Rapid onset leaves little time for evacuation; structural damage is often catastrophic
  • CFIT: High-speed impact with terrain is rarely survivable; typically occurs without warning
  • Engine Failure: Provides more time for emergency procedures; modern aircraft can fly on remaining engines
  • Weather: Outcomes vary widely based on severity and crew response

Data Evidence: Box plots show Fire/Explosion and CFIT have higher median fatalities and fewer low-fatality outliers.

Implication:

  • Prevention strategies should prioritize high-severity causes (CFIT warning systems, fire suppression)
  • Mitigation strategies should focus on improving survivability for all cause types

Pattern 4: Temporal Safety Improvements¶

Finding: Decade-over-decade reduction in both accident frequency and severity.

Explanation:

  • Regulatory Evolution: FAA, ICAO, and national authorities have strengthened standards
  • Technological Advancement: TCAS (collision avoidance), GPWS (ground proximity warning), weather radar
  • Industry Learning: Systematic investigation and implementation of lessons learned
  • Improved Maintenance: Better inspection protocols and predictive maintenance
  • Training Evolution: CRM, simulator training, recurrent training requirements

Quantitative Evidence: Recent decades show lower median fatalities and fewer extreme outliers compared to earlier periods.

Implication: Continued investment in safety technology, training, and regulatory oversight yields measurable, sustained results. The safety culture must be maintained and continuously improved.

Anomalies Discovered¶

This section highlights unusual patterns and outliers that warrant special attention.

Observation: Several accidents show fatalities far exceeding typical ranges for their cause category.

Possible Explanations:

  • Large Commercial Aircraft: Modern wide-body aircraft carry 300-500+ passengers
  • Ground Casualties: Crashes in populated areas (buildings, neighborhoods)
  • Multiple Aircraft: Mid-air collisions involving two or more aircraft
  • Secondary Disasters: Building collapse, secondary explosions, cascading failures
  • Passenger Capacity Growth: Aircraft size has increased over decades

Examples of High-Outlier Scenarios:

  • Tenerife airport disaster (1977): 583 fatalities - two 747s collided on runway
  • 9/11 attacks (2001): Deliberate crashes with building casualties
  • Japan Airlines Flight 123 (1985): 520 fatalities - largest single-aircraft accident

Investigation Priority: These outliers warrant detailed case studies to identify unique risk factors and prevent recurrence.

Implication: As aircraft capacity increases, the potential consequences of individual accidents grow, requiring even higher safety standards.

Anomaly 2: Unknown Causes Persistence¶

Observation: A significant number of accidents remain classified as "Unknown Cause" despite investigation efforts.

Possible Explanations:

  • Insufficient Wreckage Recovery: Ocean crashes, deep water, remote locations
  • Complete Destruction: Flight recorders destroyed or never recovered
  • Investigation Resources: Inadequate funding or expertise in some jurisdictions
  • Complex Failures: Multi-system failures difficult to reconstruct
  • Time Elapsed: Older accidents investigated with less sophisticated techniques

Notable Examples:

  • Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 (2014): Aircraft disappeared, never found
  • Various ocean crashes where black boxes were not recovered

Implication:

  • Investment in investigation technology (underwater recovery, enhanced recorders, satellite tracking)
  • International cooperation for investigation resources
  • Improved flight recorder technology (longer battery life, deployable recorders)

Concern: Unknown causes prevent learning and implementing preventive measures, potentially allowing similar accidents to recur.

Anomaly 3: Low-Fatality High-Risk Causes¶

Observation: Some accidents with typically severe causes (Fire/Explosion, CFIT) show surprisingly low fatalities or even zero fatalities.

Possible Explanations:

  • Ground Fires Before Takeoff: Successful evacuation before flight
  • Effective Emergency Response: Quick action by crew and emergency services
  • Fire Containment Systems: Working as designed to isolate fire
  • Small Aircraft: Fewer occupants at risk
  • Fortunate Circumstances: Crash location, time of day, weather conditions favorable for rescue
  • Partial CFIT: Glancing impact rather than direct collision

Positive Insight:

  • Demonstrates effectiveness of safety systems when properly implemented
  • Shows value of emergency training and evacuation procedures
  • Highlights importance of aircraft design (fire-resistant materials, evacuation slides)

Examples:

  • Engine fires detected early and extinguished
  • CFIT with controlled descent allowing crew to regain control
  • Successful emergency landings after fire detection

Implication: These "near-miss" scenarios provide valuable lessons for improving survivability even in high-risk situations.

Anomaly 4: Weather Accidents in Modern Era¶

Observation: Weather remains a significant contributing factor despite advanced forecasting and detection technology.

Possible Explanations:

  • Human Decision-Making Failures: Pressure to maintain schedules overrides safety concerns
  • Unexpected Phenomena: Microbursts, wind shear, clear air turbulence difficult to predict
  • Icing Conditions: Not adequately detected or communicated
  • Pilot Overconfidence: Reliance on technology without proper judgment
  • Economic Pressure: Airlines face financial penalties for delays/cancellations
  • Localized Weather: Conditions can change rapidly in small areas

Specific Weather Challenges:

  • Thunderstorms and microbursts during takeoff/landing
  • Icing on wings and engines
  • Low visibility (fog, snow)
  • Strong crosswinds exceeding aircraft limits
  • Wind shear (sudden changes in wind speed/direction)

Implication:

  • Technology alone is insufficient; must be coupled with sound decision-making culture
  • Need for better communication between meteorologists and flight crews
  • Organizational culture must support "no-go" decisions without penalty
  • Enhanced training on weather-related decision making

Key Insight: The persistence of weather-related accidents suggests a gap between available technology and its effective use in operational decision-making.

Conclusions & Recommendations¶

Summary of Findings¶

Based on our comprehensive analysis of aviation accident data, we have identified several critical patterns and anomalies:

1. Flight Phase Risk

  • Takeoff and landing are disproportionately dangerous phases requiring focused safety interventions
  • These phases account for the majority of accidents despite representing minimal flight time
  • Enhanced procedures and training for these critical phases can yield significant safety improvements

2. Contributing Factors

  • Weather and Loss of Control dominate accident causes
  • Multiple factors typically contribute to each accident (chain of events)
  • Addressing single factors in isolation is insufficient for comprehensive safety improvement

3. Fatality Patterns

  • Certain causes (Fire/Explosion, CFIT) are inherently more deadly with higher median fatalities
  • Other causes (Engine Failure, Weather) show greater variability in outcomes
  • Outliers represent catastrophic scenarios requiring special prevention strategies

4. Temporal Trends

  • Overall safety has improved significantly over decades
  • Median fatalities have decreased in recent decades
  • Despite improvements, catastrophic accidents still occur, indicating persistent risks

5. Anomalies

  • Extreme outliers highlight the potential for mass-casualty events
  • Persistent "unknown causes" indicate investigation limitations
  • Weather-related accidents despite advanced technology suggest human factors in decision-making
  • Some high-risk scenarios result in low fatalities, demonstrating effectiveness of safety systems

Recommendations¶

Immediate Actions (0-12 months)¶

1. Enhanced Training Programs

  • Focus Areas: High-risk flight phases (takeoff/landing procedures)
  • Skills Development: Loss-of-control recovery techniques and upset recovery training
  • Decision Making: Weather-related go/no-go decision protocols
  • Crew Resource Management: Enhanced communication and teamwork training
  • Simulator Training: Realistic scenarios combining multiple risk factors

2. Technology Deployment

  • Weather Systems: Expand use of predictive weather analytics and real-time updates
  • Terrain Awareness: Implement advanced GPWS (Ground Proximity Warning Systems)
  • Fire Safety: Enhanced fire detection and suppression systems
  • Flight Recorders: Deployable/ejectable black boxes for over-water flights
  • Satellite Tracking: Real-time aircraft position monitoring

3. Operational Procedures

  • Decision Protocols: Strengthen go/no-go decision-making frameworks
  • Crew Coordination: Improve crew resource management procedures
  • Emergency Response: Standardize emergency procedures across operators
  • Maintenance Checks: Enhanced pre-flight and routine inspection protocols
  • Weather Minimums: Review and potentially raise weather minimums for operations

Long-Term Strategies (1-5 years)¶

1. Data-Driven Safety

  • Investigation Capabilities: Expand accident investigation resources and technology
  • Predictive Analytics: Implement machine learning for risk assessment and prediction
  • Data Sharing: Create international databases for safety data sharing
  • Near-Miss Reporting: Encourage and analyze near-miss incidents for early warning
  • Trend Analysis: Continuous monitoring of emerging safety trends

2. Regulatory Evolution

  • Standards Updates: Revise regulations based on emerging patterns and new technology
  • International Harmonization: Align safety regulations across jurisdictions
  • Retrofit Requirements: Mandate advanced safety systems on older aircraft
  • Certification Standards: Strengthen aircraft and operator certification requirements
  • Enforcement: Ensure consistent enforcement of safety regulations

3. Cultural Change

  • Safety-First Culture: Promote organizational cultures that prioritize safety over schedule/profit
  • Reporting Culture: Reduce fear of punishment for reporting safety concerns
  • Schedule Pressure: Address economic pressures that compromise safety decisions
  • Leadership Commitment: Ensure executive-level commitment to safety
  • Industry Collaboration: Foster information sharing and collective learning

4. Research Investment

  • Outlier Studies: Detailed analysis of extreme cases for unique insights
  • Investigation Technology: Develop better tools for accident reconstruction
  • Human Factors: Research decision-making under pressure and stress
  • Emerging Risks: Study new technologies (drones, electric aircraft) for safety implications
  • Survivability: Research ways to improve crash survivability

Specific Recommendations by Pattern/Anomaly¶

For Flight Phase Vulnerability:

  • Develop phase-specific checklists and procedures
  • Increase simulator training time for takeoff/landing scenarios
  • Improve airport infrastructure (longer runways, better lighting)
  • Implement enhanced approach and departure procedures

For Multi-Factor Causation:

  • Train crews to recognize and break accident chains
  • Implement system-wide safety management systems (SMS)
  • Use scenario-based training that combines multiple risk factors
  • Develop better tools for real-time risk assessment

For High-Severity Causes:

  • Prioritize prevention of CFIT through terrain awareness systems
  • Enhance fire detection and suppression technology
  • Improve emergency evacuation procedures and equipment
  • Research crash-resistant fuel systems

For Unknown Causes:

  • Invest in underwater search and recovery technology
  • Mandate improved flight recorder technology (longer battery, deployable units)
  • Expand satellite tracking coverage
  • Increase international cooperation on investigations

For Weather-Related Accidents:

  • Develop better decision-support tools for weather assessment
  • Create organizational cultures that support weather-related delays
  • Improve communication between meteorologists and flight operations
  • Enhance pilot training on weather phenomena and decision-making

Final Thoughts¶

This comprehensive analysis of aviation accident data demonstrates that aviation safety is a complex, multi-dimensional challenge requiring continuous attention and improvement. While significant progress has been made over the decades, the persistence of certain patterns and the emergence of new anomalies indicate that complacency is not an option.

Key Insights¶

Progress is Real: The data clearly shows that aviation has become safer over time through:

  • Technological advancement
  • Regulatory improvements
  • Enhanced training
  • Industry-wide learning from accidents

Challenges Remain: Despite improvements, several persistent challenges require ongoing attention:

  • Human factors in decision-making
  • Weather-related accidents
  • Catastrophic potential of individual incidents
  • Unknown causes limiting learning opportunities

Multi-Layered Approach Required: The data reveals that most accidents are preventable through a combination of:

  • Better Technology: Advanced warning systems, improved aircraft design
  • Improved Training: Realistic scenarios, decision-making skills, CRM
  • Sound Decision-Making: Culture that supports safety over schedule
  • Robust Safety Culture: Organization-wide commitment to safety
  • Continuous Learning: Systematic analysis and implementation of lessons learned

The Path Forward¶

By addressing the patterns and anomalies identified in this report, the aviation industry can continue its trajectory toward ever-improving safety outcomes. This requires:

  1. Sustained Investment: In technology, training, and investigation capabilities
  2. Cultural Commitment: Safety must remain the top priority at all organizational levels
  3. Data-Driven Decisions: Use analytics and evidence to guide safety improvements
  4. International Cooperation: Share data, best practices, and lessons learned globally
  5. Continuous Improvement: Never assume "good enough" - always seek to improve

The ultimate goal is not just to reduce accident rates, but to eliminate preventable accidents entirely. While this may never be fully achievable, the pursuit of this goal drives continuous improvement and saves lives.

def generate_summary_statistics(dataframe, column_name):
    """
    Generate comprehensive summary statistics for a given column.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    dataframe : pandas.DataFrame
        The dataset to analyze
    column_name : str
        Name of the column to summarize
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict : Dictionary containing various statistics
    """
    stats = {
        'count': dataframe[column_name].count(),
        'mean': dataframe[column_name].mean(),
        'median': dataframe[column_name].median(),
        'std': dataframe[column_name].std(),
        'min': dataframe[column_name].min(),
        'max': dataframe[column_name].max(),
        'q25': dataframe[column_name].quantile(0.25),
        'q75': dataframe[column_name].quantile(0.75),
        'iqr': dataframe[column_name].quantile(0.75) - dataframe[column_name].quantile(0.25),
        'skewness': dataframe[column_name].skew(),
        'kurtosis': dataframe[column_name].kurtosis()
    }
    return stats


def identify_outliers(dataframe, column_name, method='iqr'):
    """
    Identify outliers in a column using IQR or Z-score method.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    dataframe : pandas.DataFrame
        The dataset to analyze
    column_name : str
        Name of the column to check for outliers
    method : str
        'iqr' for Interquartile Range or 'zscore' for Z-score method
    
    Returns:
    --------
    pandas.DataFrame : Subset of dataframe containing outliers
    """
    if method == 'iqr':
        Q1 = dataframe[column_name].quantile(0.25)
        Q3 = dataframe[column_name].quantile(0.75)
        IQR = Q3 - Q1
        lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
        upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
        outliers = dataframe[(dataframe[column_name] < lower_bound) | 
                            (dataframe[column_name] > upper_bound)]
    elif method == 'zscore':
        from scipy import stats
        z_scores = np.abs(stats.zscore(dataframe[column_name].dropna()))
        outliers = dataframe[z_scores > 3]
    
    return outliers


def compare_groups(dataframe, group_column, value_column):
    """
    Compare statistics across different groups.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    dataframe : pandas.DataFrame
        The dataset to analyze
    group_column : str
        Column to group by
    value_column : str
        Column to calculate statistics for
    
    Returns:
    --------
    pandas.DataFrame : Summary statistics by group
    """
    comparison = dataframe.groupby(group_column)[value_column].agg([
        'count', 'mean', 'median', 'std', 'min', 'max'
    ]).round(2)
    
    return comparison

def export_summary_report(dataframe, filename='summary_report.txt'):
    """
    Export a comprehensive text summary of the dataset.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    dataframe : pandas.DataFrame
        The dataset to summarize
    filename : str
        Output filename
    """
    with open(filename, 'w') as f:
        f.write("AVIATION ACCIDENT DATA ANALYSIS - SUMMARY REPORT\n")
        f.write("=" * 70 + "\n\n")
        
        f.write(f"Dataset Shape: {dataframe.shape}\n")
        f.write(f"Total Accidents: {len(dataframe)}\n")
        f.write(f"Date Range: {dataframe['Date'].min()} to {dataframe['Date'].max()}\n\n")
        
        f.write("FATALITY STATISTICS\n")
        f.write("-" * 70 + "\n")
        f.write(f"Total Fatalities: {dataframe['Fatalities'].sum():.0f}\n")
        f.write(f"Mean Fatalities per Accident: {dataframe['Fatalities'].mean():.2f}\n")
        f.write(f"Median Fatalities per Accident: {dataframe['Fatalities'].median():.2f}\n\n")
        
        f.write("ACCIDENTS BY FLIGHT PHASE\n")
        f.write("-" * 70 + "\n")
        phase_counts = dataframe['Accident_Phase'].value_counts()
        for phase, count in phase_counts.items():
            f.write(f"{phase}: {count} ({count/len(dataframe)*100:.1f}%)\n")
        
        f.write("\n" + "=" * 70 + "\n")
        f.write("Report generated successfully!\n")
    
    print(f"Summary report exported to: {filename}")

    """
    Generate and save all visualizations in batch.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    dataframe : pandas.DataFrame
        The dataset to visualize
    output_dir : str
        Directory to save visualizations
    """
    import os
    
    # Create output directory if it doesn't exist
    if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
        os.makedirs(output_dir)
    
    print(f"Generating visualizations in: {output_dir}/")
    
    # Visualization 1: Flight Phase
    ts = dataframe["Accident_Phase"].value_counts()
    plt.figure(figsize=(10,5))
    sns.barplot(x=ts.index, y=ts.values, hue=ts.index, palette="Purples_r", legend=False)
    plt.title("Accidents by Flight Phase")
    plt.xticks(rotation=30, ha='right')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(f'{output_dir}/01_flight_phase.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close()
    print("  ✓ Flight phase visualization saved")
    
    # Visualization 2: Contributing Factors
    factor_counts = pd.Series({
        "Weather": dataframe["Weather_Involved"].sum(),
        "Engine Failure": dataframe["Engine_Failure"].sum(),
        "Loss Of Control": dataframe["Loss_of_Control"].sum(),
        "CFIT": dataframe["CFIT"].sum(),
        "Fire/Explosion": dataframe["Fire_Explosion"].sum(),
        "Unknown": dataframe["Unknown_Cause"].sum()
    })
    plt.figure(figsize=(10,5))
    sns.barplot(x=factor_counts.index, y=factor_counts.values, hue=factor_counts.index, 
                palette="viridis", legend=False)
    plt.title("Contributing Factors")
    plt.xticks(rotation=30, ha='right')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(f'{output_dir}/02_contributing_factors.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close()
    print("  ✓ Contributing factors visualization saved")
    
    # Visualization 3: Fatalities by Cause
    plt.figure(figsize=(12,6))
    sns.boxplot(data=dataframe, x="Primary_Cause", y="Fatalities", 
                hue="Primary_Cause", legend=False)
    plt.title("Fatalities by Primary Cause")
    plt.xticks(rotation=30, ha='right')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(f'{output_dir}/03_fatalities_by_cause.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close()
    print("  ✓ Fatalities by cause visualization saved")
    
    # Visualization 4: Temporal Trends
    plt.figure(figsize=(14,6))
    sns.boxplot(data=dataframe, x="Decade_Label", y="Fatalities", 
                hue="Decade_Label", legend=False)
    plt.title("Fatality Distribution by Decade")
    plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(f'{output_dir}/04_temporal_trends.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close()
    print("  ✓ Temporal trends visualization saved")
    
    print(f"\nAll visualizations saved successfully in: {output_dir}/")


# Example usage
print("Exporting summary report...")
export_summary_report(df_clean, 'aviation_analysis_summary.txt')

print("\nExporting all visualizations...")
export_visualizations_batch(df_clean, 'analysis_visualizations')

def run_complete_analysis(dataframe, export_results=True):
    """
    Execute complete aviation accident analysis pipeline.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    dataframe : pandas.DataFrame
        The cleaned dataset
    export_results : bool
        Whether to export results to files
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict : Dictionary containing all analysis results
    """
    results = {}
    
    print("="*70)
    print("AVIATION ACCIDENT ANALYSIS PIPELINE")
    print("="*70)
    
    # 1. Basic Statistics
    print("\n[1/6] Calculating basic statistics...")
    results['total_accidents'] = len(dataframe)
    results['total_fatalities'] = dataframe['Fatalities'].sum()
    results['date_range'] = (dataframe['Date'].min(), dataframe['Date'].max())
    print(f"  ✓ Analyzed {results['total_accidents']} accidents")
    
    # 2. Flight Phase Analysis
    print("\n[2/6] Analyzing accidents by flight phase...")
    results['phase_counts'] = dataframe['Accident_Phase'].value_counts()
    print(f"  ✓ Identified {len(results['phase_counts'])} flight phases")
    
    # 3. Contributing Factors
    print("\n[3/6] Analyzing contributing factors...")
    results['factor_counts'] = pd.Series({
        "Weather": dataframe["Weather_Involved"].sum(),
        "Engine Failure": dataframe["Engine_Failure"].sum(),
        "Loss Of Control": dataframe["Loss_of_Control"].sum(),
        "CFIT": dataframe["CFIT"].sum(),
        "Fire/Explosion": dataframe["Fire_Explosion"].sum(),
        "Unknown": dataframe["Unknown_Cause"].sum()
    })
    print(f"  ✓ Analyzed {len(results['factor_counts'])} contributing factors")
    
    # 4. Fatality Analysis
    print("\n[4/6] Analyzing fatality distributions...")
    results['fatality_by_cause'] = dataframe.groupby('Primary_Cause')['Fatalities'].describe()
    results['fatality_outliers'] = identify_outliers(dataframe, 'Fatalities')
    print(f"  ✓ Identified {len(results['fatality_outliers'])} outlier cases")
    
    # 5. Temporal Analysis
    print("\n[5/6] Analyzing temporal trends...")
    results['decade_stats'] = dataframe.groupby('Decade_Label')['Fatalities'].describe()
    results['accidents_by_decade'] = dataframe.groupby('Decade_Label').size()
    print(f"  ✓ Analyzed trends across {len(results['decade_stats'])} decades")
    
    # 6. Export Results
    if export_results:
        print("\n[6/6] Exporting results...")
        export_summary_report(dataframe, 'complete_analysis_report.txt')
        export_visualizations_batch(dataframe, 'complete_analysis_visualizations')
        print("  ✓ All results exported")
    else:
        print("\n[6/6] Skipping export (export_results=False)")
    
    print("\n" + "="*70)
    print("ANALYSIS COMPLETE!")
    print("="*70)
    
    return results


# Run the complete analysis
analysis_results = run_complete_analysis(df_clean, export_results=True)

# Display key findings
print("\n\nKEY FINDINGS SUMMARY:")
print("-" * 70)
print(f"Total Accidents Analyzed: {analysis_results['total_accidents']}")
print(f"Total Fatalities: {analysis_results['total_fatalities']}")
print(f"\nMost Common Flight Phase: {analysis_results['phase_counts'].index[0]}")
print(f"Most Common Contributing Factor: {analysis_results['factor_counts'].idxmax()}")
print(f"Number of Extreme Outliers: {len(analysis_results['fatality_outliers'])}")
